In [[mathematics]], '''Müger's theorem''' asserts that the [[Center (category theory)|Drinfeld center]] of every [[Spherical category|spherical]] [[fusion category]] is a [[modular tensor category]]. Müger's theorem was introduced in 2003 by mathematician Michael Müger.<ref name=":12">{{Cite journal |last=Müger |first=Michael |date=2003-05-01 |title=From subfactors to categories and topology II: The quantum double of tensor categories and subfactors |url=https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0022404902002487 |journal=Journal of Pure and Applied Algebra |volume=180 |issue=1 |pages=159–219 |doi=10.1016/S0022-4049(02)00248-7 |issn=0022-4049|url-access=subscription }}</ref> Due to the connections between spherical fusion categories and modular tensor categories to the [[algebraic theory of topological quantum information]], this theorem has found various uses within [[mathematical physics]].

== Interpretation in terms of topological quantum field theory ==
In terms of topological quantum field theory, Müger's theorem is useful for understanding the relationship between the Turaev–Viro construction and the [[Reshetikhin–Turaev invariant|Reshetikhin–Turaev construction]]. The Reshetikhin–Turaev construction takes as input a modular tensor category and has as output a (2+1)-dimensional [[topological quantum field theory]].<ref name=":3">{{Cite journal |last1=Reshetikhin |first1=N. |last2=Turaev |first2=V. G. |date=1991-12-01 |title=Invariants of 3-manifolds via link polynomials and quantum groups |url=https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/BF01239527 |journal=Inventiones Mathematicae |language=en |volume=103 |issue=1 |pages=547–597 |bibcode=1991InMat.103..547R |doi=10.1007/BF01239527 |issn=1432-1297|url-access=subscription }}</ref> The Turaev–Viro construction takes as input a spherical fusion category and has as output a (2+1)-dimensional topological quantum field theory.<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Turaev |first1=V. G. |last2=Viro |first2=O. Y. |date=1992-10-01 |title=State sum invariants of 3-manifolds and quantum 6j-symbols |journal=Topology |volume=31 |issue=4 |pages=865–902 |doi=10.1016/0040-9383(92)90015-A |issn=0040-9383}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Barrett |first1=John |last2=Westbury |first2=Bruce |date=1996 |title=Invariants of piecewise-linear 3-manifolds |journal=Transactions of the American Mathematical Society |language=en |volume=348 |issue=10 |pages=3997–4022 |doi=10.1090/S0002-9947-96-01660-1 |issn=0002-9947 |s2cid=47992659}}</ref> The relationship between these models is that the Turaev–Viro model with input spherical fusion category <math>\mathcal{C}</math> is equivalent to the Reshetikhin-Turaev model with input modular tensor category <math>\mathcal{Z}(\mathcal{C})</math>.<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Barrett |first1=John W. |last2=Faria Martins |first2=João |last3=García-Islas |first3=J. Manuel |date=2007-09-01 |title=Observables in the Turaev–Viro and Crane–Yetter models |journal=Journal of Mathematical Physics |language=en |volume=48 |issue=9 |page=093508 |arxiv=math/0411281 |bibcode=2007JMP....48i3508B |doi=10.1063/1.2759440 |issn=0022-2488 |s2cid=17561704}}</ref> For this to be a valid equivalence, it is necessary for the Drinfeld center of a spherical fusion category to be a modular tensor category.

== Interpretation in terms of the Levin–Wen model ==
In terms of [[Lattice model (physics)|lattice model]], Müger's theorem is useful for understanding the Levin–Wen model. In [[condensed matter physics]], the Levin–Wen model is a construction which takes as input a unitary fusion category <math>\mathcal{C}</math> and has as output an [[exactly solvable]] lattice model for [[topological order]] whose [[anyon]]s are described by the category <math>\mathcal{Z}(\mathcal{C})</math>.<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Levin |first1=Michael A. |title=String-net condensation: A physical mechanism for topological phases |date=2004-04-27 |last2=Wen |first2=Xiao-Gang|journal=Physical Review B |volume=71 |issue=4 |article-number=045110 |doi=10.1103/PhysRevB.71.045110 |arxiv=cond-mat/0404617 }}</ref> For <math>\mathcal{Z}(\mathcal{C})</math> to be a valid description of anyons in a physical system, the [[algebraic theory of topological quantum information]] asserts that <math>\mathcal{Z}(\mathcal{C})</math> would need to be a [[unitary modular tensor category]].

Every unitary fusion category <math>\mathcal{C}</math> admits a canonical [[Spherical category|spherical]] structure.<ref name=":2">{{Cite book |last1=Etingof |first1=Pavel |title=Tensor Categories |last2=Gelaki |first2=Shlomo |last3=Nikshych |first3=Dmitri |last4=Ostrik |first4=Viktor |publisher=American Mathematical Society |year=2015}}</ref> As such, Müger's theorem applies and asserts that <math>\mathcal{Z}(\mathcal{C})</math> is a [[modular tensor category]], and the unitary structure on <math>\mathcal{C}</math> endows <math>\mathcal{Z}(\mathcal{C})</math> with the structure of a [[unitary modular tensor category]]. Thus, in this context, Müger's theorem encodes the fact that for any unitary fusion category <math>\mathcal{C}</math> the quantum double <math>\mathcal{Z}(\mathcal{C})</math> is a valid choice of anyon theory for the Levin–Wen model.
